## Overview

This vignette demonstrates `decontamSensitivity` using the analysis structure
from a published healthy-volunteer skin microbiome study. It evaluates a series
of prevalence thresholds without automatically selecting an optimal value.

The input phyloseq object is external to the package. The code below is not
evaluated while the package vignette is built; set `HV_PHYLOSEQ_RDS` to an
authorized local copy before running it.

## Load the input object

```{r load-data, eval=FALSE}
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)
library(decontamSensitivity)

input_path <- Sys.getenv("HV_PHYLOSEQ_RDS")
stopifnot(nzchar(input_path), file.exists(input_path))

ps <- readRDS(input_path)
stopifnot(
  inherits(ps, "phyloseq"),
  "T.C" %in% sample_variables(ps),
  "Control" %in% as.character(sample_data(ps)$T.C),
  "Genus" %in% rank_names(ps)
)
```

This workflow uses the control-status field to define biological samples and
negative controls.

## Run the complete threshold workflow

```{r run-qc, eval=FALSE}
qc <- run_decontam_qc(
  ps = ps,
  control_column = "T.C",
  control_label = "Control",
  thresholds = seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1),
  taxonomy = "Genus",
  group_colors = c(
    total = "black",
    biological = "tomato",
    control = "steelblue"
  ),
  progress = TRUE
)

qc
```

The OTU-table orientation is read from the phyloseq object. Every supplied
threshold produces summary tables, plots, and a filtered phyloseq object.

```{r inspect-output, eval=FALSE}
qc$tables$threshold_summary
qc$tables$sample_retention_summary
qc$tables$flagged_taxa

qc$plots$threshold_sensitivity
qc$plots$sample_retention
qc$plots$flagged_taxa_reads_by_threshold[["0.1"]]

ps_filtered_01 <- qc$filtered_phyloseq_by_threshold[["0.1"]]
```

## Create the flagged-taxa animation

The animation uses a long-format table. Taxa are ranked independently at every
threshold, while the displayed read axis is fixed to the global maximum so the
plot area does not shift between frames.

```{r animation-code, eval=FALSE}
library(gganimate)

flagged <- qc$tables$flagged_taxa
n_biological <- sum(!qc$result$is_control)
n_control <- sum(qc$result$is_control)

flagged_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    threshold = flagged$threshold,
    taxon = flagged$taxon,
    group = "Biological samples",
    reads = flagged$reads_biological / n_biological
  ),
  data.frame(
    threshold = flagged$threshold,
    taxon = flagged$taxon,
    group = "Negative controls",
    reads = flagged$reads_control / n_control
  )
)

top_n <- 15L
taxon_rank <- aggregate(reads ~ threshold + taxon, flagged_long, sum)
taxon_rank$rank <- ave(
  -taxon_rank$reads,
  taxon_rank$threshold,
  FUN = function(x) rank(x, ties.method = "first")
)
taxon_rank <- taxon_rank[taxon_rank$rank <= top_n, ]

flagged_long <- merge(
  flagged_long,
  taxon_rank[, c("threshold", "taxon", "rank")],
  by = c("threshold", "taxon")
)
threshold_levels <- format(qc$thresholds, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE)
flagged_long$threshold_label <- factor(
  format(flagged_long$threshold, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE),
  levels = threshold_levels
)
taxon_rank$threshold_label <- factor(
  format(taxon_rank$threshold, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE),
  levels = threshold_levels
)
global_read_max <- max(flagged_long$reads, na.rm = TRUE)

p_animation <- ggplot(
  flagged_long,
  aes(
    x = rank,
    y = reads,
    fill = group,
    group = interaction(taxon, group)
  )
) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_text(
    data = taxon_rank,
    aes(x = rank, y = 0, label = taxon, group = taxon),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 1.15,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_x_reverse(
    limits = c(top_n + 0.5, 0.5),
    breaks = seq_len(top_n),
    labels = NULL
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, global_read_max * 1.12),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Biological samples" = "tomato",
    "Negative controls" = "steelblue"
  )) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean raw reads per sample",
    fill = NULL,
    title = "Flagged taxa reads — threshold {current_frame}"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.2),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(linewidth = 0.1),
    text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 10, 190)
  ) +
  transition_manual(threshold_label)

animation <- animate(
  p_animation,
  nframes = 45,
  fps = 5,
  width = 1000,
  height = 700,
  units = "px",
  res = 96,
  device = "png",
  end_pause = 10,
  renderer = gifski_renderer()
)

anim_save("flagged_taxa_reads_by_threshold.gif", animation)
```

## Create a before/after animation

The threshold-specific plots returned by `run_decontam_qc()` retain the
long-format plot data. These data can be combined without exposing metadata
columns that are unrelated to QC.

```{r before-after-animation-code, eval=FALSE}
parts <- lapply(names(qc$plots$taxa_reads_before_after_by_threshold), function(th) {
  x <- qc$plots$taxa_reads_before_after_by_threshold[[th]]$data
  data.frame(
    threshold = as.numeric(th),
    sample = as.character(x$Sample),
    taxon = as.character(x$taxon_plot),
    state = ifelse(grepl("^Before", as.character(x$state)), "Before", "After"),
    sample_group = as.character(x$sample_group),
    reads = x$Abundance
  )
})
before_after_long <- do.call(rbind, parts)

# Replace sample labels before exporting a public animation.
sample_key <- setNames(
  sprintf("Sample_%03d", seq_along(unique(before_after_long$sample))),
  unique(before_after_long$sample)
)
before_after_long$sample <- unname(sample_key[before_after_long$sample])

# Build the stacked-bar animation with transition_manual(threshold).
# Use a fixed read scale when stable panel geometry is required.
```

## Interpretation

The sensitivity plots should be interpreted together. A useful threshold
reduces control-associated reads while preserving biological reads, samples,
and plausible taxa. Sample-level distributions are important because aggregate
retention can conceal substantial losses in individual samples. Intermediate
animation frames are display states, not additional decontam analyses.

## Reference

The study context is described in the
[published Scientific Reports analysis](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-62903-7#Sec17).
Analyses using contaminant scores should also cite the original `decontam`
method listed in the package README.
